question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? According to research by Bing Xie and her colleagues, plains zebras produce at least four kinds of vocalizations: "snorts," "soft snorts," "squeals," and "quagga quagga" calls. To ______ the recordings they had gathered according to type, the team relied on machine-learning algorithms; this analysis showed that snorts differ from one zebra to the next, whereas squeals stay fairly consistent across zebra populations.
option a: collapse
option b: categorize
option c: suppress
option d: extend
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Machine learning was used to sort the recordings by type, so 'categorize' fits.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "considered" most nearly mean? This passage comes from Chinua Achebe's 1964 novel Arrow of God, which is set in Nigeria during the 1920s. Ezeulu, the religious leader for several villages, declares when the yearly yam harvest may begin.
Whenever Ezeulu considered the immensity of his power over the year and the crops—and thus over the people themselves—he questioned whether it was genuine. He did name the day for the feast of the Pumpkin Leaves and for the New Yam feast, yet he did not select it. He was nothing more than a watchman. His authority amounted to no more than a child's authority over a goat that people called his own.
©1964 by Chinua Achebe
option a: Respected
option b: Anticipated
option c: Pondered
option d: Allowed
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Ezeulu is reflecting on the scope of his power, so 'considered' means pondered.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The source of the silver in European coins minted from the 600s into the early 800s CE has long been a matter of scholarly dispute. A geochemical study by Kershaw et al. examining 49 coins dating to 660-820 CE offers solid evidence that settles two rival hypotheses: the earliest coins drew on Byzantine silver, while the later ones relied on Frankish silver—findings that supply firm details in what had previously been a ______ area of study.
option a: authoritative
option b: speculative
option c: esoteric
option d: solitary
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The new evidence brings firm details to an area that had been speculative.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? In the effort to locate new impact craters on Mars, seismic monitoring and orbital imaging serve as ______ sources of data: once vibrations picked up by seismic monitoring reveal roughly where an impact took place, researchers can examine orbital photographs of that comparatively small stretch of rocky terrain to pinpoint the new crater exactly.
option a: complementary
option b: interchangeable
option c: exhaustive
option d: redundant
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The two data sources work together, so they are complementary.

question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text? Knowing how juvenile sea turtles migrate is essential for conservation work. Although adult sea turtles have been studied thoroughly, far less is understood about juveniles during their oceanic phase, a period they spend largely in the open sea. To gain insight into this phase, researchers fitted six juvenile green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas) with tags and released them into the eastern Caribbean Sea. Their data showed that most of the turtles simply drifted along with the region's ocean currents, though two individuals swam against the currents—perhaps searching for feeding areas off the coast of South America.
option a: To propose explanations for why certain juvenile sea turtles swim against ocean currents
option b: To describe conservation programs for sea turtles that have succeeded
option c: To summarize research on a little-studied phase of sea turtle development
option d: To contrast how adult and juvenile sea turtles behave while migrating
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text summarizes new research on juveniles' understudied oceanic stage.

question: Which choice best states the function of the underlined sentence? Magical realism—a mode that blends the fantastical into otherwise realistic stories—took shape in Latin America during the 1960s. It is linked to Gabriel García Márquez, whose Big Mama's Funeral stands as a central text. Mexican American authors took up the style as well; Rudolfo Anaya, for instance, drew fantastical material from Mexican folktales in Bless Me, Ultima. Even so, Anaya's Tortuga contains no fantastical events. And notwithstanding his popular reputation, García Márquez himself produced several strictly realist works, among them Love in the Time of Cholera.
option a: To suggest that Mexican American writers whom García Márquez influenced may have, in turn, shaped his own work
option b: To dispute the widespread belief that Big Mama's Funeral surpasses García Márquez's realist writing
option c: To correct the potential impression that every one of García Márquez's works followed magical realism
option d: To point out an overlooked similarity between Love in the Time of Cholera and Bless Me, Ultima
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence corrects the impression that García Márquez always wrote magical realism.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Writing in a portion of a 1976 essay on United States film, James Baldwin observed that Lady Sings the Blues (1972)—a biographical film about the jazz singer Billie Holiday—could be said to reflect Holiday's life and the experiences of Black Americans only "by courtesy." For Baldwin, the movie's inability to portray its subject truthfully pointed to a broader pattern in the period's films: rather than using the medium's capacity to grapple with hard truths, studios and filmmakers frequently fell back on comforting platitudes about contemporary US society.
option a: It conveys Baldwin's dismissal of the era's US cinema in favor of older films that portray society more authentically.
option b: It characterizes the nature of the disconnect Baldwin identified between reality and how it was represented in US cinema.
option c: It presents a view of Baldwin's that the text says diverged sharply from the consensus held by US film critics.
option d: It expresses Baldwin's first reaction to a US film that the text implies he would later reconsider.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: It characterizes the disconnect Baldwin saw between reality and its portrayal in film.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Microwave heating is a thermal method used to preserve food on an industrial scale, and it is generally regarded as superior to more traditional thermal preservation approaches. Scientists in Latin America have advanced understanding of the technology; researchers in Brazil, for instance, demonstrated that it works well for preserving mango peels. Going forward, scientists hope to develop hybrid systems that pair several food-preservation technologies—an approach that would improve on microwave heating used by itself, since that method frequently heats food unevenly.
option a: It suggests a benefit that microwave heating offers over conventional thermal processing methods.
option b: It identifies a flaw of microwave heating technologies.
option c: It explains why conventional thermal processing methods are widely used in commercial applications.
option d: It introduces microwave heating as a technology for processing food.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Uneven heating is named as a flaw of microwave heating.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the sentence?
Percentage of US Congress Members Who Self-Identified as Veterans, 1953-2023 (bar graph showing the House of Representatives and the Senate for the years 1953, 1973, 1993, 2003, 2013, and 2023; the y-axis, Percent, runs from 0 to 80).
From the country's earliest days, both chambers of the United States Congress have included many military veterans among their elected members, such as Hiram L. Fong (a veteran of the US Army Air Force) and Ralph Harold Metcalfe Sr. (a veteran of the US Army). After compiling historical figures on members of Congress who reported prior military service, a research institute concluded that ______
option a: the percentage of those members decreased substantially in both houses of Congress from 1973 to 2013.
option b: from 2003 to 2023, the House of Representatives had a higher percentage of those members than the Senate did.
option c: the percentage of those members remained fairly consistent, regardless of house, from 1993 to 2023.
option d: from 1953 to 2003, those members constituted a majority in both houses of Congress.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The graph shows a substantial decline in both chambers from 1973 to 2013.

question: Which quotation from The Man in the Brown Suit most effectively illustrates the claim? The Man in the Brown Suit, a 1924 novel by Agatha Christie, follows the protagonist Anne Beddingfeld, who describes how strongly her father disliked living in the present era, saying, ______
option a: "[Papa's] mind dwelt in Palaeolithic times, and the inconvenience of life for him was that his body inhabited the modern world."
option b: "The opinion of other people never interested [Papa] in the slightest degree."
option c: "Although [Papa] was a fellow of almost every important society, and had rows of letters after his name, the general public scarcely knew of his existence."
option d: "In a few minutes Papa stalked off."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The quote about his mind dwelling in Palaeolithic times shows his dislike of the modern era.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the student's conclusion?
Average Hours Worked per Person per Year in 1950 and 2017
Country | 1950 | 2017 | Change in hours | Percent change in hours
Peru | 2,157 | 1,932 | -225 | -10%
Argentina | 2,034 | 1,692 | -342 | -17%
Australia | 2,178 | 1,731 | -447 | -21%
Ireland | 2,419 | 1,746 | -674 | -28%
Calculations may be inexact due to rounding.
For an economics class, a student is examining why the average number of hours a person works each year has fallen since 1950 across several nations—a drop attributed both to rising productivity and to the adoption of policies that cap working hours. As a first step, the student wants to see how Argentina's decline compares with those of the other countries. The student finds that ______
option a: the percent decrease in hours worked was greater in Argentina than it was in Ireland, Australia, or Peru.
option b: though the decline in number of hours worked in Argentina was less than that in Ireland and Australia, it was greater than that in Peru.
option c: while the number of hours worked rose in Argentina between 1950 and 2017, it declined in Ireland, Australia, and Peru.
option d: though the decline in number of hours worked in Argentina was greater than that in Ireland and Peru, it was less than that in Australia.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Argentina's decline was smaller than Ireland's and Australia's but larger than Peru's.

question:
Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' conclusion?
Across subtropical Asia, Apis dorsata (the giant honeybee) is vital for pollinating a wide range of crops and wild plants. To examine how various agricultural land covers affect the species, Rika Raffiudin and colleagues tracked the bees' foraging activity and analyzed the pollen in the honey from A. dorsata colonies at two Indonesian sites: Kampar, ringed by monoculture farms (each growing a single crop), and Kerinci, a forest-agriculture location where several crops—hot peppers and coffee among them—are grown nearby. The team concluded that limited crop variety may reduce the total amount of pollen A. dorsata gathers.
option a: Pollen in honey samples from Kampar bee colonies was predominantly sourced from a single plant species, whereas pollen in honey samples from Kerinci bee colonies was sourced from multiple different plant species.
option b: Honey samples from Kerinci bee colonies contained significantly higher concentrations of pollen than honey samples from Kampar bee colonies did.
option c: In one Kerinci bee colony, a greater proportion of bees returned to their nests with pollen than returned without pollen, whereas the inverse was observed in a second Kerinci bee colony.
option d: Significantly fewer bees were observed engaging in foraging activities with the crops surrounding Kerinci than with the crops surrounding Kampar.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Higher pollen concentration at crop-diverse Kerinci supports the conclusion.

question:
Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researcher's claim?
The Rarámuri language of northern Mexico uses 20 vowel and consonant sounds, while the Taa language of southern Africa uses more than 100. What explains such a difference? One researcher proposes that when modern humans first arose in Africa, they spoke a single language, but as people gradually spread across Africa and then around the globe, that language branched into new languages. These, in turn, split into still more languages as small bands of humans migrated even farther, with each newly formed language preserving fewer of the sounds found in humanity's original language.
option a: A wider range of sounds is found across the languages of Africa as a whole than across the languages of South America as a whole.
option b: The number of sounds is fairly consistent across the various languages that emerged in the last parts of Africa to be settled by humans.
option c: Languages that emerged in Europe and Western Asia tend to have more sounds than languages that emerged in Africa do.
option d: Languages that emerged in Central America tend to have fewer sounds than languages that emerged in Western Europe do, and Central America is farther away from Africa than Western Europe is.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: More sounds in far-flung Europe/Western Asia than in Africa contradicts the claim.

question:
Which choice most logically completes the text?
Every kind of stainless steel contains varying amounts of iron, carbon, and corrosion-resisting chromium. Ferritic stainless steel, often used for cooking utensils, contains a greater share of chromium (at least 10.5%) than austenitic stainless steel does, along with more iron, which gives it its magnetic properties. Austenitic stainless steel, by contrast, has a face-centered cubic crystalline structure produced by adding nickel to the alloy. It comes in two subtypes: the 200 series, frequently used for home water tanks, and the 300 series, which contains more nickel than the 200 series and is often used for furnaces or for mining and chemical equipment. It follows that stainless steel used to manufacture ______
option a: cooking utensils will have a face-centered cubic crystalline structure.
option b: mining and chemical equipment will have a concentration of chromium lower than 10.5%, while stainless steel used to manufacture home water tanks will not.
option c: furnaces will have similar magnetic properties to stainless steel used to manufacture cooking utensils.
option d: home water tanks will have a lower percentage of chromium in its composition than stainless steel used for cooking utensils will.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Water-tank (austenitic) steel has less chromium than utensil (ferritic) steel.

question:
Which choice most logically completes the text?
Outi Tervo and her team investigated how human-caused noise affects narwhals (Monodon monoceros), Arctic marine mammals that are highly sensitive to changes in the sounds around them. Suspecting that elevated sound levels disrupt narwhal foraging, the team compared the animals' diving behavior under natural sound conditions with their behavior under two human-caused sound conditions—ship sounds alone, and ship sounds combined with sonic pulses. Relative to natural conditions, both exposure conditions produced significant reductions in the number and target depth of the deep dives associated with foraging. The diving behaviors under the two exposure types, however, differed negligibly—an outcome that could be attributed to the fact that ______
option a: the narwhals weren't as sensitive to human-caused sounds as the researchers had predicted.
option b: sonic pulses can be heard at significantly greater ocean depths than ship sounds can.
option c: narwhals forage at shallower depths in the presence of ship sounds alone than in the presence of ship sounds coupled with sonic pulses.
option d: ship sounds contribute so much to the overall sound level that the addition of sonic pulses has little effect on the narwhals' auditory environment.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Ship sounds dominate, so adding sonic pulses barely changes the sound environment.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Hong Kong's Temple Street Night Market, a public market, ______ operating decades ago. It remains active today, drawing shoppers who seek everything from street food to handmade textiles and gifts.
option a: began
option b: will begin
option c: begins
option d: would begin
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: An action completed decades ago requires the past tense 'began.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? One of the more than 120 photographs in the 2021 exhibition The New Woman Behind the Camera, Olga Máté's ______ "Fisherman's Dock" offers a glimpse back in time to 1930.
option a: photograph
option b: photograph;
option c: photograph:
option d: photograph,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between the noun 'photograph' and the title it introduces.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Adopted in 1868, Luxembourg's 5,601-word constitution—unlike Belgium's, which was adopted in 1831 and runs to a far larger 16,119 words—______ as the 9th shortest in the world. Constitutional scholars such as Giovanni Sartori study data like these and use them to draw broader conclusions.
option a: ranks
option b: have ranked
option c: rank
option d: are ranking
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular subject 'constitution' takes the singular present-tense verb 'ranks.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Heather Sarsons, a behavioral economist at the University of British Columbia, studies how psychological factors (such as emotion and bias) shape the economic decisions that individuals ______ Sarsons's research also considers the broader effects those decisions have on the economy.
option a: make, moreover,
option b: make; moreover,
option c: make, moreover;
option d: make, moreover.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon must separate the two independent clauses before the adverb 'moreover.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To evaluate the biodiversity of Amsterdam's urban forest, a 2024 study cataloged all of the city's trees. After finding that administrative unit GM16 had a native-to-non-native tree ratio of 0.66, the researchers ______ efforts to improve the biodiversity of that unit's trees and of other areas with a similarly moderate ratio.
option a: having recommended
option b: to recommend
option c: recommended
option d: recommending
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence needs a finite past-tense main verb, 'recommended.'
